page.layout: Top: running head with page number at the upper left. Full width: a two-column table ("Theorematis" left, "Problematis" right) with numbered rows, then an ornament rule. Then a centred chapter heading. Below it: left margin with four or five notes, and one main text column of paragraphs, with a short line-broken paragraph at the foot continuing onto the next page. No text below the main column.

main_text.l: 1. Finis est speculatio. | Finis est opus aliquod, ut pictura trianguli, inscriptio circuli.
2. Demonstratio petitur ex axiomatis. | Demonstratio petitur è postulatis.
3. Enunciatio est hypothe-tica, Si: ut, si fuerit triangulum. | Enunciatio fit per infini-tivū:ut, circulo quadratum inscribere.
4. Clausula est: quod de-mōstrasse oportuit. | Clausula est: quod fe-cisse oportuit.

l.i: Exempla peti possunt ex Euclide, & aliis Mathe-maticis.

head.i: Cap. 9. Sententia Francisci Junii de principiis.

main_text.p: Archelogia accuratissimi Theologi, Francisci Junii.Videamus nunc sententiam Francisci Junii de Principiis, quam expressit in libro de politia Mosis observatione.
Principium essendi & cognoscendi.Principium est vel essendi, ut Deus; vel co-gnoscendi. Principium cognoscendi est re-gula recta omnis cognitionis.
Principium cognoscendi aeternum.Estq; vel æternum; puta conceptus immuta-bilis formaq; rationis in Deo principe Universitatis existens ante omnia tempora; aut informatum & traditum in tempore.
Principium cognoscendi in tempore estQuod in tempore,aut principium natura-le est, aut naturæ adveniens.
I. Naturale.Principium naturale est, quod veluti inna-tum creaturis ratione præditis, informat eas notionibus naturæ communibus, aliquâ par-ticipa-

page.notes: Ornamental rule between the table and the chapter heading is not text and is left out. Initial "V" of "Videamus" is a joined drop cap; read as V from the form "Ideamus". Uncertain readings: "de-mōstrasse" (the letters after "de-" are hard to read; the macron may be over o or n; written as printed-looking with no [?]; treat with care), "aliquâ" (circumflex uncertain), "præditis" (the "æ" ligature is faint). Italic extent in the table rows is approximate. Column/row layout of the table is read as parallel columns. No catchword or signature is visible at the foot. Show-through from the facing page is not transcribed.
